memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now the people of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know what the Lord said to Moses the man of God at Kadesh Barnea about you and me. I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the Lord sent me from Kadesh Barnea to explore the land. And I brought him back a report according to my convictions" - Josh 14:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now one of the most stirring figures in the whole book steps forward: Caleb. Decades earlier, he had been one of the twelve spies sent to explore the Promised Land. Ten came back terrified, focused on the giants. Only Caleb and Joshua came back trusting God. Here, all these years later, Caleb reminds Joshua of a promise God made back then — a promise he has carried in his heart the whole time.

Notice how Caleb describes his younger self: he brought back a report "according to my convictions." While others reported what their fears told them, Caleb reported what his faith told him. He saw the same giants the others saw, but he measured them against God rather than against himself. Conviction shaped his words when fear shaped everyone else's.

Caleb had been waiting on this promise for forty-five years. Think of that patience — nearly half a century of holding onto something God had said, through wilderness wandering and war, never letting go. His example asks us a searching question: are we willing to trust God's word over the long haul, even when fulfilment is slow in coming? The God who kept His promise to Caleb across all those years is faithful still, and the hope we have in Christ will never put us to shame (Rom 5:5).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you let your convictions or your fears shape how you speak about your challenges?
- Is there a promise of God you have grown tired of waiting for?
- How does Caleb's forty-five years of patient trust encourage you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me the faith of Caleb — to see my challenges in light of Your greatness, and to hold onto Your word patiently, however long the waiting. Amen.
